subject.title: [Feature]: Add gateway-side circuit breaker for unhealthy sessions after consecutive failures

question: Should OpenClaw add a core session-health circuit breaker for all no-progress session failures, and what default action, receipt shape, and config surface should it expose?
rationale: The remaining work is not just counting attempts; it would establish public session-health semantics, persistence, user recovery actions, UI/log events, and optional config/default behavior that affect existing runtime and operator workflows.

options.title: Design a narrow core session-health receipt first
options.body: Add a first-class receipt and default pause/manual-recovery path, then layer thresholds and optional auto-rotation only after the contract is explicit.

options.title: Extend only the existing idle-timeout breaker
options.body: Broaden the current helper to count more no-progress attempt classes, accepting that UI/session-health receipts and auto-rotation remain separate follow-up work.

options.title: Keep targeted guards only
options.body: Continue addressing retry storms through narrower idle-timeout, compaction, tool-loop, provider, and subagent issues instead of creating a general session breaker now.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow core session-health receipt first
recommendation.body: Add a first-class receipt and default pause/manual-recovery path, then layer thresholds and optional auto-rotation only after the contract is explicit.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses current agent-runtime architecture, public config, and product recovery UX, and steipete has the strongest recent history on the broad runner/runtime surface.
